sections.label: Small Claims Tribunal consumer claims
sections.summary: Consumers can file claims against businesses at the Small Claims Tribunal, which hears cases up to $10,000, or $20,000 if both parties agree.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Consumers are also able to file claims against businesses with the Small Claims Tribunal (SCT), which hears cases of up to $10,000, or $20,000 if both the consumer and the business agree.

sections.label: Voluntary compliance agreements with businesses
sections.summary: The CPFTA lets CASE and the Singapore Tourism Board make voluntary compliance agreements with errant businesses to stop unfair practices and compensate consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The CPFTA empowers CASE and the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) to enter into voluntary compliance agreements (VCAs) with errant businesses to stop them from engaging in unfair practices, and to compensate aggrieved or affected consumers.

sections.label: Gap in injunction process
sections.summary: The review found a gap in the current injunction process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The review found that there is a gap in the current injunction process.

sections.label: SPRING Singapore as administering agency
sections.summary: SPRING Singapore, a Statutory Board under MTI, is to be appointed administering agency for the CPFTA with investigation and enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING Singapore) is a Statutory Board under MTI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: It is to be appointed as the administering agency for the CPFTA with investigation and enforcement powers.

sections.label: SPRING Singapore investigation and injunction powers
sections.summary: Clauses 4, 5 and 8 give SPRING Singapore investigation powers and make it the only entity able to submit injunction applications under the CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 8 inserts a new Part 3A on investigation powers to be conferred on SPRING Singapore to obtain information, enter premises which it reasonably believes are being used for unfair practices, and to gather evidence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 4 which amends section 9 on declaration or injunction, and clause 5 which repeals and re-enacts new section 10, empower SPRING Singapore as the only entity under the CPFTA to submit injunction applications against errant businesses to the Courts.

sections.label: Refunds for breaching Court orders
sections.summary: Entities breaching accompanying Court orders must refund consumers who cancel their contracts within six months of the transaction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Entities that breach such accompanying Court orders will be required to refund consumers who cancel their contracts within six months of the transaction.

sections.label: Court measures and contempt
sections.summary: Courts may impose measures like publicising injunction orders for a period capped at five years, extendable to 10 years; non-compliance is contempt of Court, a criminal offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The additional measures that the Courts may impose, such as publicising of the injunction orders, are for compliance over a specified period, which is to be decided by the Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: This period is currently capped at five years but may be extended by the Courts to 10 years if the errant business or individual fails to comply in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Failure to comply with a Court order is a contempt of Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: This is a criminal offence which could result in a fine and/or imprisonment.

sections.label: Clause 10 unfair practices definitions
sections.summary: Clause 10 amends the Second Schedule of the CPFTA to clarify unfair practice definitions, supporting SPRING Singapore's investigation and enforcement, drawing on other jurisdictions and CASE's feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: In addition to the two main amendments, clause 10 amends the Second Schedule of the CPFTA to clarify the definitions of the unfair practices to support SPRING Singapore's investigation and enforcement and make clear to businesses and consumers on what really constitutes unfair practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The amendments are referenced from consumer protection legislation in other jurisdictions and will take in CASE's feedback such as making clear that it is an unfair practice to refuse to give a consumer a copy of a written agreement if it was previously not given to the consumer.

sections.label: Proposed CPFTA changes
sections.summary: The proposed CPFTA changes address errant retailers, strengthen measures against persistent unfair practices, prevent sidestepping injunction orders, and raise consumer awareness for informed purchasing decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The proposed changes to the CPFTA address the issue of errant retailers, strengthens the spectrum of measures that may be taken against such businesses which persist in unfair practices, prevent errant businesses from sidestepping injunction orders, and more importantly, raise consumers' awareness of unfair practices and errant businesses so that they can make informed purchasing decisions.

sections.label: Injunction power moves to SPRING
sections.summary: The amendments remove injunction power from CASE and STB, appointing SPRING Singapore as administrative agency with investigation and enforcement powers; CASE entered 20 VCAs and six injunctions since 2004.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: With the proposed amendments, the power to take injunction action would be removed from CASE and STB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: SPRING Singapore will be appointed as the administrative agency for the CPFTA with powers to investigate and to enforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Ever since the CPFTA took effect in 2004, CASE has entered into 20 VCAs and taken out six injunctions against retailers who had breached the CPFTA.

sections.label: Injunction against abetting suppliers
sections.summary: The proposed Bill includes a clause 10 provision for the Court to grant an injunction restraining a person from knowingly abetting, aiding, permitting or procuring a supplier to engage in an unfair practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: They should understand the severe consequence for breaching the CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I am also pleased that the proposed Bill includes a provision at clause 10 for the Court to grant an injunction restraining a person from knowingly abetting, aiding, permitting or procuring a supplier to engage in an unfair practice.

sections.label: Assurance on referring wrongdoing
sections.summary: The question seeks the Minister of State's assurance that SPRING Singapore would refer evidence of criminal conduct found during investigation to the Police for prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Page: 72 So, may I seek an assurance from the Minister of State that if SPRING Singapore discovers evidence of criminal conduct during the course of investigation, they would not hesitate to refer the wrongdoing to the Police for prosecution?

sections.label: Contempt proceedings against retailers
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister of State to assure that SPRING Singapore will take contempt proceedings against retailers breaching a Court order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Likewise, if retailers act in breach of the Court order, can I seek the Minister of State's assurance that SPRING Singapore will take up contempt proceedings against such retailers?

sections.label: California Fitness liquidation and prepayments
sections.summary: The speaker cites California Fitness's liquidation, noting it had negative equity of $21.7 million in January 2015 yet kept selling platinum memberships and collecting prepayments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The latest company closure which adversely affected consumers is the liquidation of California Fitness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I read the report by the provisional liquidators, and I was appalled that even though the company was clearly in negative equity position of $21.7 million as at January 2015, the company continued to sell platinum memberships and collect prepayments from their customers.

sections.label: Disallowing compulsory arbitration clauses
sections.summary: The speaker proposes disallowing compulsory arbitration clauses for claims below $10,000, since such clauses oust the SCT's jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Consumers also cannot turn to the SCT for help due to the arbitration clause, which ousts the jurisdiction of SCT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, one option, if I may propose, is to disallow compulsory arbitration clauses if it relates to claims below $10,000, which is similar to the limit for SCT.

sections.label: Power to enter premises without warrant
sections.summary: Clause 12(i) of the Bill provides that in an investigation under section 12(g)(i), the authority may enter premises without a Court warrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 12(i) of the Bill provides that in connection with an investigation under section 12(g)(i), the authority may have a power to enter premises without a Court warrant.

sections.label: Requiring Court warrant first
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether officers should be required to seek a Court warrant first in all cases, as in clause 12(j).

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would it not be more appropriate to require officers to seek a Court warrant first in all the cases, just like in clause 12(j)?

sections.label: CASE CaseTrust Accreditation Scheme
sections.summary: The speaker says term packages can benefit businesses and customers, and notes CASE's CaseTrust Accreditation Scheme covers businesses such as renovation companies, employment agencies, spas and travel agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Such term packages can often be a win-win deal for both businesses and customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am aware that CASE has the CaseTrust Accreditation Scheme which covers certain businesses, for example, renovation companies, employment agencies, spas and travel agencies.

sections.label: Voluntary secured payment scheme
sections.summary: The Government could consider a scheme letting retailers from all industries voluntarily adopt secured payment or performance bond practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Alternatively, the Government maybe should consider starting a scheme to encourage and allow retailers from all industries and not just those who have signed up with CaseTrust to voluntarily opt for a secured payment or performance bond practice.

sections.label: SPRING Singapore as administering agency
sections.summary: Appointing SPRING Singapore to administer the Act with investigation powers and powers to require errant retailers to publicise injunctions strengthens measures against rogue traders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed appointment of SPRING Singapore to be the administering agency for the Act, with powers to investigate and require errant retailers to publicise that they are under injunction, will help to strengthen the measures that may be taken against rogue traders and service providers engaged in unfair trading practices.

sections.label: Renovation industry unfair practices
sections.summary: The speaker hopes SPRING Singapore will consider publishing a blacklist of renovation contractors with contact details to help consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Unfair practices in the renovation industry are especially painful for consumers because the sums involved could run into tens of thousands of dollars and it may cost as much to fix a poorly renovated flat as doing everything from scratch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope that SPRING Singapore will look into the possibility of publishing a list of blacklisted renovation contractors together with their contact details such that consumers have more information when deciding on which renovation contractor to appoint.

sections.label: Internet blacklist of errant businesses
sections.summary: The speaker hopes SPRING Singapore can consider publishing a blacklist of errant businesses on the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Page: 76 I hope SPRING Singapore can consider publishing a blacklist of these errant businesses on the Internet.

sections.label: Enforcement on timeshare and online retailers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Bill can be enforced on timeshare companies and online retailers, noting pre-1 April 2014 agreements are not covered by CPFTA cancellation amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I would like to know whether this Bill, when passed, could be enforced on timeshare companies and online retailers selling goods and subscription services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, these agreements were signed before 1 April 2014, and they are not covered under the amendments to the CPFTA pertaining to cancellation of contracts.

sections.label: Children unknowingly subscribing in mobile games
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Court will compel online retailers to publicise injunctions if SPRING Singapore finds them guilty of deceiving customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With the availability of many free mobile games that advertise subscription for paid services or some weekly lucky draws, consumers, especially vulnerable young children, playing these games using their parents' mobile devices may unknowingly subscribe to such services or lucky draws which come with recurring weekly or monthly charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Will the Court also compel these online retailers to publicise that they are under injunction should investigation by SPRING Singapore find them guilty Page: 77 of deceiving customers?

sections.label: Amendment and non-business customers
sections.summary: The amendment addresses a gap and underpins the relationship between businesses and their non-business customers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By addressing this gap, the present amendment represents an important change that will underpin the relationship that businesses have with their non-business customers.

sections.label: SPRING Singapore investigative enforcement powers
sections.summary: The speaker urges addressing root causes of negative practices and appointing SPRING Singapore with investigative and enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Rather than plugging each loophole as it arises or seeking to have an ironclad protection from the get-go, it may be better to address the development of such negative practices by looking at what are the root causes giving rise to them within our business ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is why the appointment of SPRING Singapore, with its experience and scope, is so important.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the assignment of investigative and enforcement powers to SPRING Singapore, one area which I would urge the agency tasked with the new role to look into is whether the occurrences of claims and conflicts are synchronised with the general state of the economy, and, if so, whether they tend to increase or decrease as the economy weakens.

sections.label: Authority over business ecosystem flaws
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the agency can address ecosystem flaws and whether stringent enforcement could worsen challenges for small businesses in weak economies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will it also be given the authority to address flaws or weaknesses in the business ecosystem, if its investigation of cases reveals that there are, for instance, perverse incentives which fuel the growth of poor business practices?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, in relation to whether the frequency of claims and conflict arising from consumer protection legislation is closely tied to the business cycle, I would like to ask whether the Ministry has considered the issue of whether stringent enforcement could exacerbate the challenges faced by businesses, especially the small ones, during times when the economy is weak.

sections.label: Support for consumer protection Bill
sections.summary: The speaker states full support for the Bill to strengthen laws to better protect consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this regard, I stand in full support of this Bill to strengthen our laws to better protect consumers.

sections.label: Protecting vulnerable group and tourists
sections.summary: The speaker asks what else protects this vulnerable group and assures tourists Singapore is a safe shopping haven, calling the Bill about lost trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what else is being done to protect this vulnerable group, as well as steps to assure prospective tourists that Singapore remains a safe shopping haven?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Page: 80 Lastly, most people I have spoken to about this Bill simply label it as a Bill that will give us peace of mind when we shop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But it really is a Bill about trust lost in our society.

sections.label: Trust in cohesive society
sections.summary: A high level of trust indicates an integrated, resilient and cohesive society requiring less Government intervention and fewer laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A high level of trust is indicative of an integrated, resilient and cohesive society, one which will require less Government intervention and fewer laws.

sections.label: Trust and moral values
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Singapore focuses on community spirit and trust, cultivated by protecting society's moral fabric, not just physical safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There is no doubt we are a safe society and our primary focus should be our physical safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But I hope we can focus not only on our physical safety but also on our community spirit and continue to build a society where a higher level of trust exists amongst all of Page: 81 us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The trust that holds society together like glue cannot, and should not, be lost in our search for economic progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And this trust can only be cultivated by protecting the moral fabric of our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These are my high hopes for Singapore – strong moral values which guide our behaviour, without the constant need for Government carrots and sticks.

sections.label: SPRING Singapore consumer redress
sections.summary: Under the amendment, SPRING Singapore will not provide redress or compensation to consumers of errant retailers, who must seek legal action themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, under this amendment and according to the frequently asked questions released by MTI in May this year, SPRING	Singapore will not be responsible specifically for providing redress or compensation to consumers who are victims of errant retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Rather, those consumers will need to find redress through legal action that they undertake and finance themselves or with the help of CASE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is a huge concern because many consumers refrain from taking legal action even in the SCT due to their lack of experience with the legal system and concerns about time and cost.

sections.label: Escalating action for repeat offenders
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether there will be an escalating scale of severity of action for repeat offenders, including individuals setting up successive companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Seventh, will there be an escalating scale of severity of action taken in the case of repeat offenders, who may be companies or, as the Minister of State observed, individuals, to set up successive companies to cover their tracks?

sections.label: Retail and F&B sales rise
sections.summary: Retail sales rose 1.4% in May 2016 over the previous month, and F&B services sales increased 0.9%.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Retail sales, seasonally adjusted, rose by 1.4% in May 2016 over the previous month.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Sales of food and beverage (F&B) services increased 0.9% in May 2016 over the previous month.

sections.label: California Fitness liquidation
sections.summary: California Fitness recently went into liquidation.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Just recently, we saw California Fitness go into liquidation.

sections.label: CaseTrust for prepaid services
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether all fitness gyms, beauty salons and wellness spas selling prepaid services should be required to come under CaseTrust.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah(Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Should all fitness gyms, beauty salons and wellness spas be required to come under CaseTrust, if they are selling prepaid services?

sections.label: Singapore retail industry size
sections.summary: The retail industry comprises over 16,000 firms, from microenterprises and SMEs to international fashion houses and large department stores.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The retail industry in Singapore is large and highly variegated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It comprises more than 16,000 firms, from microenterprises and small and medium enterprises to international fashion houses and large department stores, offering consumers access to a wide range of goods and services.

sections.label: CASE and CDCs outreach
sections.summary: From this month, CASE will work with five Community Development Councils over three years on consumer education talks for heartlanders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With effect from this month, CASE will also work with the five Community Development Councils over the next three years to roll out consumer education talks and reach out to heartlanders.

sections.label: CaseTrust accreditation scheme
sections.summary: The voluntary CaseTrust scheme requires participating businesses to have good service practices and, for certain schemes, prepayment protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The voluntary CaseTrust accreditation scheme requires participating businesses to have good service practices, and for certain schemes, involve prepayment protection.

sections.label: Enhancing CPFTA protections
sections.summary: Enhancing the CPFTA strengthens measures against errant retailers to give consumers greater protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By enhancing the CPFTA we are strengthening the measures that may be taken against errant retailers to give greater protection to consumers.

sections.label: Three-pronged consumer protection approach
sections.summary: CPFTA penalises errant businesses, and consumers, industry and Government each have roles in a three-pronged approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Besides protecting consumers' interest, CPFTA can also penalise those errant businesses to safeguard the reputation of the retail and service industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Page: 86 Everyone has a role to play by staying alert to those errant businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We can adopt a three-pronged approach, that is, consumers, the industry and the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, the industry should put more effort into training or set up professional accreditation bodies to increase the service awareness and standard of the retailers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, on the part of the Government, we pass legislation, such as CPFTA, to further ensure that we provide a level playing field for all businesses to compete fairly, so that customers can buy with peace of mind the products they like and the service they need.

sections.label: Bill amendments and SPRING Singapore
sections.summary: The Bill appoints SPRING Singapore as administering agency with investigation and enforcement powers, and adds court-imposed measures on errant businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The key amendments to the Bill, that is, to appoint SPRING Singapore as the administering agency with investigation and enforcement powers to gather evidence and file injunction applications with the Courts against errant retailers and to introduce additional measures which Page: 87 may be imposed by the Courts on errant businesses are a welcome move as Singapore prides itself to be a popular tourism destination.

sections.label: CASE mediation claim cap
sections.summary: The claim amount for CASE mediation is capped at $30,000, and the speaker suggests reviewing and raising this limit as goods costs rise.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current amount of claim is capped at $30,000 for those who seek CASE mediation.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I suggest this limit to be reviewed and raised in tandem, especially when the cost of goods is increasing over time.

sections.label: Online transaction complaint statistics
sections.summary: CASE statistics showed 159 complaints on online transactions last year, compared to 146 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Five, CASE statistics showed that the complaints filed on online transactions were 159 last year, compared to 146 in 2014.

sections.label: Awareness programmes for retailers
sections.summary: Retailers under injunction should attend awareness programmes on sales ethics, and this should be compulsory even before company registration.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, retailers under injunction should be made to go for awareness programmes to know their "do"s and "don't"s or ethics of sales of goods or services to consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For that matter, even before a company is registered, this must be made compulsory.

sections.label: Labelling retailers under injunction
sections.summary: Retailers under injunction should be clearly and visibly labelled so consumers, especially tourists, are aware and avoid follies.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, we should clearly and visibly label retailers under injunction so that consumers especially tourists, are aware and will not fall into any follies.

sections.label: Notices of declaration or injunction
sections.summary: Suppliers must display a notice of declaration or injunction in premises and on their website, and the speaker seeks clarification on the term "individual".

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: One is to require the supplier to display prominently in the premises a notice that a declaration has been issued or an injunction granted against the supplier; and two, is to require the supplier to include on its website a notice of the declaration or injunction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, for sections 9(4)(e) and (f), I seek clarification on what is meant by the term "individual"?

sections.label: Agents classified as suppliers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether "agents" who procure items from another source and sell directly to customers can be classified as suppliers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Can these "agents" also be classified as suppliers since they procure the items for the customers from another source and sells directly to the customers, bearing in mind that these so-called "agents" are not agents nor are they representatives of the foreign suppliers?

sections.label: Extension of specified period
sections.summary: Asks whether the specified period can be extended beyond 10 years for a recalcitrant supplier who did not comply with an order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, a recalcitrant supplier has been imposed with the maximum 10 years and during the last one or two years, he did not comply with an order under sections 9(4)(a) to (d) or sections 9(4)(e) or (f), can there be an extension of the specified period to more than 10 years under this provision?

sections.label: Jover Chew cheating case
sections.summary: Mr Jover Chew was sentenced to 33 months' imprisonment for cheating over $16,000 from 26 victims at a Sim Lim Square mobile phone shop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The case of Mr Jover Chew, who was sentenced to 33 months' imprisonment last year for cheating over $16,000 from 26 victims, most of them foreign workers and tourists, while operating a mobile phone shop in Sim Lim Square made international news in neighbouring countries and was widely shared on social media.

sections.label: Courts ordering retailers to publicise
sections.summary: One key proposed amendment would give Courts power to order errant retailers to publicise that they are under an injunction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One of the key proposed amendments is for the Courts to have the power to order errant retailers to publicise that they are under an injunction.

sections.label: Sudden business closures concern
sections.summary: A third concern is sudden business closures that impact consumers, particularly in the fitness and beauty industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My third concern is the sudden business closures that impact consumers, particularly in the fitness and beauty industries.

sections.label: Customers losing money on closures
sections.summary: Customers lose their hard-earned money when a gym or salon closes suddenly, like California Fitness recently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While such business models are not illegal, customers will lose their hard-earned money when a gym or a salon closes down suddenly, much like what happened with California Fitness recently.

sections.label: Consumer protection recurring review
sections.summary: The Bill would stop unscrupulous retailers opening multiple outlets, give STB wide investigative powers, and let Courts require errant retailers to notify consumers of injunction orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, in this fast-moving modern age, I feel consumer protection is one topic which will need a recurring review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am pleased that the Bill would put a stop to the practice of unscrupulous retailers who open multiple outlets so that they can continue with their malpractices after they are caught.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The new section under 12(G) would give STB and its investigation officers very wide-ranging investigative powers, from pursuing the culprits to seizing their goods for investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The amendment also gives the Court the powers to require the errant retailers to notify consumers that it is under an injunction order.

sections.label: Publicity and SPRING Singapore role
sections.summary: Calls for wide publicity on where to report errant retailers, with SPRING Singapore as administering agency for faster action and easier redress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There should be wide publicity so that the public knows where they can go to to make reports against errant retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Now that SPRING Singapore will be the administering agency after the Bill is passed, it would hopefully allow for faster action to be taken and for consumers to be aware about the types of unfair practices and are able to seek redress more easily with one single agency.

sections.label: Limit advance payment periods
sections.summary: Requests the Bill limit advance payments for services contracts to not more than six calendar months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Another point I would like to raise is my request that the Bill limit the period in which companies can ask a consumer to sign for advanced payment for services contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We should limit all such payments to not more than six calendar months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Operators should not ask clients to sign for packages that last for so long and lure them with discounts.

sections.label: Owners stop marketing, scam alerts
sections.summary: Says owners should be required by law to stop marketing when financially in dire straits, and suggests SPRING Singapore alert platform for scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While the frontline sales staff may not know the financial health of the company, the owners should be required by law to stop any further marketing once they know they Page: 93 are financially in dire straits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Maybe SPRING Singapore could look into having a certain platform where people can be alerted to scammers, including foreign ones, so that at least the buyers can get some form of warning.

sections.label: Bill reduces loopholes
sections.summary: Says the Bill is a welcome improvement with fewer loopholes, ensuring dishonourable operators cannot escape enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Other Members in this House have pointed this out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, in this context, the Bill is a welcome improvement: making sure there are fewer loopholes, ensuring that dishonourable operators cannot escape enforcement.

sections.label: Cooling-off period for prepaid packages
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will consider a cooling-off period for prepaid packages, especially those with large upfront payments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Even if a copy of the contract is provided to the customer, it may be too late to seek justice once the contract has been signed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, will the Ministry consider introducing a cooling-off period for prepaid packages, especially those involving large amounts of payment upfront?

sections.label: Bill fairer marketplace for consumers
sections.summary: Says the Bill is a positive, progressive step towards a fairer marketplace, benefiting those most in need of protection.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Overall, this Bill is a positive step towards a fairer and more equitable marketplace for consumers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is a progressive policy, because those who benefit most are those most in need of protection – those who are less well-informed, less literate, less aware of the industry norms and buyer experience.

sections.label: Unfair contract terms list
sections.summary: Mr Lim Biow Chuan suggested the CPFTA regulations include a list of unfair contract terms, such as mandatory arbitration for consumer disputes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan has suggested that the regulations under the CPFTA include a list of unfair contract terms, such as requiring that all consumer disputes be referred to arbitration.

sections.label: California Fitness prepayment protection
sections.summary: Five Members highlighted the California Fitness closure and asked if the Government can do more to protect consumer prepayments, such as limiting prepayments to six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Mr Melvin Yong, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Saktiandi Supaat have highlighted the recent case of the closure of California Fitness and asked if the Government can do more to protect consumer prepayments, such as limiting the amount of prepayments that businesses can collect to just six months.

sections.label: Broad-based prepayment measure challenging
sections.summary: Given the wide range of businesses, imposing a broad-based measure on all businesses to protect consumers against prepayment loss from closures would be very challenging.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Given the wide range of businesses, it would be very challenging to impose a broad-based measure on all businesses to protect consumers against loss of prepayments from business closures.

sections.label: CaseTrust for prepaid packages
sections.summary: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah suggested all fitness gyms, beauty salons and wellness spas selling prepaid packages be required to come under CaseTrust.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah suggested that all fitness gyms, beauty salons and wellness spas be required to come under CaseTrust if they sell prepaid packages.

sections.label: CPFTA online and offline protection
sections.summary: CPFTA gives the same protection whether purchases are online or from a brick-and-mortar shop, and courts may require e-commerce retailers under injunctions to publicise injunction orders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: CPFTA provides the same protection to consumers, whether their purchases are made online or from a brick-and-mortar shop.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: E-commerce retailers under injunctions may be required by the courts to publicise injunction orders, such as through taking out advertisements in the print media, or on the landing pages of their website.

sections.label: CPFTA business-to-consumer scope
sections.summary: The CPFTA applies only to business-to-consumer transactions, and agents assisting local consumers to buy from foreign websites are considered suppliers subject to CPFTA measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Ms Thanaletchimi also asked if CPFTA covers consumer-to-consumer transactions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I must clarify that the CPFTA applies only to business-to-consumer transactions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Agents who carry on a business by assisting local consumers to purchase from foreign websites are considered as suppliers and they are, therefore, subject to the measures under the CPFTA if they engage in unfair business practices.

sections.label: SPRING and CASE errant business information
sections.summary: SPRING Singapore will work with CASE to give consumers information on errant businesses issued injunction orders by the Courts, including renovation contractors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: SPRING Singapore will work with CASE to make available to consumers information on errant businesses which have been issued injunction orders by the Courts, including renovation contractors.

sections.label: Injunction notification and employment changes
sections.summary: Under the proposed amended CPFTA, a retailer under injunction may be required by the Courts to notify SPRING Singapore of entity or employment changes relating to consumer transactions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Under the proposed amended CPFTA, a retailer under injunction may be required by the Courts to notify the administering agency, in this case, SPRING Singapore, of any changes to the entity or the individual's employment if the changes relate to consumer transactions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, if you are under injunction, you leave this store, you go and work in a different store, but you are still forward-facing and dealing with customers, then even if you are an employee, you need to declare, and there has to be a notice given to the customers that you are under injunction and you are still serving customers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This enables the administering agency to monitor and prevent the errant retailer from side-stepping injunction orders by closing the business and setting up a new business under a different name while persisting with the unfair practice.

sections.label: Measures against bad eggs
sections.summary: The measures would help prevent a few bad eggs from affecting an entire sector or industry, and will be set up by end of 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In challenging economic times, it is even more important that these measures would help to prevent a few bad eggs from affecting the businesses of an entire sector or industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It will be set up by the time the finalised amendments to CPFTA are operationalised towards the end of 2016.

sections.label: Referral to Police
sections.summary: If SPRING Singapore finds an errant retailer may have engaged in activities criminalised under the Penal Code, it will refer the case to the Police.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If, however, during SPRING	Singapore's investigations, SPRING	 	Singapore finds that the errant retailer may have engaged in activities criminalised under the Penal Code, SPRING Singapore will not hesitate to refer the case to the Police for further investigation.

sections.label: Search without Court warrant
sections.summary: The default position is to enact the power through a Court warrant, but urgent circumstances such as tourists harmed by an egregious retailer could justify searching premises earlier without a warrant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The default position is to enact the power through a Court warrant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But in certain circumstances in which the egregious behaviour requires more urgent action, where tourists, for example, in large numbers may be harmed or fleeced by an egregious retailer, then there could be reasons for us to enact a search of the premises to gather evidence much earlier without a Court warrant.

sections.label: SCT hearing times
sections.summary: SCT usually hears cases within a month of filing, but tourists in Singapore only briefly may opt to appear in person and be heard within 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: SCT usually hears cases within a month of filing, but tourists who are in Singapore only for a short time may opt to appear in person at SCT and be heard within 24 hours.

sections.label: Timeshare complaints dropped after tighter rules
sections.summary: Complaints on timeshare businesses filed with CASE have dropped significantly since tighter regulations were introduced in 2009 and 2014.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera and Mr Saktiandi Supaat may be assured to know that the number of complaints on timeshare businesses filed with CASE has dropped significantly since the introduction of tighter regulations on such contracts in 2009 and 2014.

sections.label: CPFTA claim limit kept at $30,000
sections.summary: Less than 1% of CASE complaints over three years exceed the $30,000 CPFTA claim limit, so the limit is maintained.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked if the claim limit under the CPFTA can be increased from $30,000 currently.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Data has shown that less than 1% of the number of complaints that CASE has received over the last three years exceeds this claim limit under the CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, we are maintaining a careful watch and do not think there is any need to adjust this number at this point in time.

sections.label: Repair or replace non-conforming goods
sections.summary: The CPFTA lets a consumer require the retailer to repair or replace goods that fail satisfactory quality within six months of purchase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Based on this, the CPFTA provides that the consumer may require the retailer to repair or to replace the goods if they fail to conform to satisfactory quality within six months of the purchase.

sections.label: MLM under CPFTA and Pyramid Selling Act
sections.summary: MLM is covered under the CPFTA and is also subject to the Multi-Level Marketing and Pyramid Selling (Prohibition) Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: MLM is covered under Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (CPFTA), but I would also like to clarify that the MLM sector is also subject to the Multi-Level Marketing and Pyramid Selling (Prohibition) Act which lays out prohibitions on the objectionable features of pyramid selling.

sections.label: Errant retailers referred to SPRING Singapore
sections.summary: CASE surfaces errant retailers who ignore a Voluntary Compliance Agreement to SPRING Singapore, which under the amended Act can gather evidence for the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: An errant retailer like Mobile Air who repeatedly carries out unfair practices and ignores the request from Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) to sign a Voluntary Compliance Agreement would be surfaced by CASE to the administering agency, in this case Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING Singapore), for further investigation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And under the new amended Act, SPRING Singapore will have the power to gather evidence, which would be submitted to the Courts.

sections.label: Renovation contractor cases referred to SPRING
sections.summary: CASE can refer a retailer with a consistent pattern of unfair practice to SPRING Singapore, regardless of the sums involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: In the case of renovation contractors, the sums are very big and it could be $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, it is not to say that you need to have a huge number of cases before action can be taken.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In the first instance, if there is an unfair business practice that the consumers have given feedback to CASE, and if CASE genuinely believes, after a few cases, that there is a consistent pattern of behaviour in a certain particular retailer and they feel strongly that there is an unfair practice going on, they can already refer this to SPRING Singapore to consider, to look and see whether there is evidence for further action to be taken.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But the quantum of the sum that is involved does not itself mean that there is egregious behaviour ongoing.
